content.text:
I reviewed the code and the options against the five criteria.

The loop starts at i = 1 and compares marks[i] with marks[i-1] for each recorded mark, so mystery() counts adjacent increases. Option A states this.

The stem says marks arrive "through record", and size caps the loop, so only recorded marks are examined. Option A also holds when fewer than two marks are recorded (the result is 0), and the first mark has no predecessor, so "recorded marks greater than the mark just before them" is accurate.

The distractors are distinct and plausible: counting all calls to record, comparing against the first mark, and counting decreases. B fails when calls are ignored or when marks decrease. C fails for sequences like 5, 3, 4. D fails for any increasing sequence.

The "why" for the key option is a weak rationale ("On every test sequence the value returned by running the method equals this description"). It is explanatory filler rather than a real reason, and it reads as generated text. It is a minor issue, but it counts against the distractor/explanation criterion.

The item tests tracing and describing behavior (skill 4.A) in topic 3.5 (writing methods that depend on object state). The code is short, the reading load is low, and there is no inheritance. Time is about 95 seconds, which is acceptable.
